subject: HarborTech expansion — combined trial credits + first‑year discount request
messages:
From: Olivia Martin <olivia.martin@harbortech.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood pilot — request for credits + pricing concession

Hi Ben —

First, thanks for the support during our POC last week. The team has been impressed with inference latency; our engineers flagged several wins compared to the previous provider. The usage spike in the last 10 days is much higher than we estimated (attached usage export).

We’re preparing an internal ask to propose Redwood as the inference partner for our new Recommendation feature. To get approval we need a commercial anchor from you: specifically a trial credits top‑up so the evaluation covers production‑scale queries and a promotional discount for first‑year committed spend. Rough ask: +$30k in trial credits and a 15% one‑time discount off year1 committed pricing. We’re prepared to sign a 12‑month committed contract immediately if we can agree to those terms.

Can you escalate for executive approval? I know this is outside standard playbooks but we think the revenue profile justifies it.

Best,
Olivia Martin
Sr. Product Manager, HarborTech
Attachment: harbortech-poc-usage.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Redwood pilot — request for credits + pricing concession

Team — forwarding HarborTech’s ask. TL;DR: asking for $30k additional trial credits + 15% first‑year discount in exchange for an immediate 12‑month commit. Deal looks like $180k ARR if they convert at our proposed committed SKUs.

Why I’m escalating: they’re strategic in our logistics vertical roadmap and the POC shows high token volumes; losing them would be noticeable in our US logistics book. Options I see:
- Approve a capped credit grant (e.g., 40% of their ask) + milestone-based release on conversion
- Approve full credits but lower discount to 10%, require 12‑month minimum and non‑cancellable clause
- Decline and offer smaller PoC extension with technical onboarding support

Attachments: redwood_proposal_v1.pdf (draft commercial); fin_margin_calc.xlsx (quick margin impact).

Requesting quick guidance — Marissa, can you recommend the commercial ask? Evelyn, request executive exception if you’re comfortable. Rishi, can you validate the margin math? Deal id: HARB-4721.

Thanks,
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T12:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood pilot — request for credits + pricing concession

Agree we should be cooperative here; HarborTech is a high-velocity prospect. My recommended structure (fastest path to sign):
- One-time trial credit grant: $20k (cap), disbursed as $10k now + $10k on conversion signature
- First‑year discount: 12% off listed committed price for a 12‑month term
- Require minimum 3.5M tokens/month or usage-based true‑up clause after 3 months

I’ve attached a redline of the term sheet with the milestones. This keeps upside for us while removing the blocker for procurement. If exec wants to be more aggressive we can push to $30k credits + 15% but only with finance pre‑approval.

—Marissa
Attachment: contract_redline_HARB-4721.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood pilot — request for credits + pricing concession

Quick margin check on Marissa’s proposal: assuming conversion to the 12‑month committed SKU at their expected runrate (~3.5M tokens/mo) — the blended unit economics with a $20k credit and 12% discount results in ~9% gross margin compression in year1 but recovers in year2 assuming standard renewal at list. If we move to $30k credits + 15% discount we drop to ~16% first‑year margin compression; that is material but manageable if we expect a 24‑month retention.

If exec approves the $30k/15% combo, I need finance to sign off on the ARR expectations and a clause for a minimum guaranteed spend (or accelerated true‑up) after month 3. See attached quick calc.

—Rishi
Attachment: fin_margin_calc.xlsx
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T08:34:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Redwood pilot — request for credits + pricing concession

Thanks for the analysis and quick turn, team. Approve an exception with the following firm caveats:
1) One‑time trial credit grant: $30,000 max (not to be exceeded).
2) First‑year discount: 15% off committed pricing, conditional on a signed 12‑month agreement with an auto‑renew clause.
3) Credits released in two tranches: $15k on signature of the commitment, $15k after successful production cutover (ops acceptance test) within 90 days.
4) Finance to insert a minimum guaranteed spend clause or accelerated true‑up at month 3 — Rishi please coordinate.
5) Legal to run a short addendum to capture the milestone release and credit recapture on early termination.

I’m authorizing this as an executive exception for HARB‑4721. Ben — proceed to finalize commercial and send DocuSign link once Legal finishes the addendum. Please keep the approval email chain for audit.

—Evelyn
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
